chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, who said:

I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding marriage, and his letter came to me in his own handwriting: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When there comes to you one whose character and religion you are pleased with, then marry him. If you do not do so, there will be fitnah (trial/strife) in the earth and great corruption.''
And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Husayn ibn Bashshar al-Wasiti, who said:

I wrote to Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him) asking him about marriage, and he wrote back (peace be upon him): 'When one proposes to you who has the religion and trustworthiness you are pleased with, then marry him. If you do not do so, there will be fitnah in the earth and great corruption.''
ai.seo_question: What are the primary conditions for accepting a marriage proposal according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from the chapter on Kafa'ah (spousal compatibility) highlights the Imam's emphasis on moral and religious integrity as the primary criteria for marriage, superseding mere lineage or wealth. It underscores the communal responsibility to facilitate unions to prevent social disorder, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the preservation of societal stability through proper marital alliances.
